I can take apart a laptop and replace parts or even revive computers and cell phones marinated in Kool-Aid or Pop, but when it comes to the OS side of things, that's where I can't attack it with a screw-driver.

The idea behind this sub is for Newbies to ask questions about several things.

  1. They could post their machine's stats like: CPU, RAM, Video Card, HDD size and get a Build and Programs that would help them make the best use of their machine.

  2. They could also post about their favorite programs/games and see if there is a way to make them work with Linux. (I like playing Civ 5 right now and love watching Netflix, but I've had problems with Getting Netflix to work in the past for example.)

  3. New Users could post problems they are having and let others help them develop their google-fu or point them to helpful forums. (I've seen somewhere that Nvidea cards have a slight problem with Linux so since I have one, that would be a good direction to point me should I choose to switch over to a Linux build.

All In all this is supposed to be a sub where I hope people can help each other. It seems that a big reason that I and others haven't switched to Linux is that with all the builds and all the options it becomes daunting to think about switching. With Windows you set-it-and-forget-it, which leads to a lazy sort of mentality. It is hoped that this place can help overcome that initial fear of being overwhelmed and makes it a little easier to be lazy in installing Linux, to gently introduce new users to the Linux environment and offer smaller steps to get the best use out of what seems to be a very enthusiastic community.

If you are a mod of a Linux sub, or a linux user and think your skills would be helpful here, please post a link or PM me. I admit I know too little about Linux to really help and welcome experienced users that are willing and able.
